comparisons.reading: Both independent models are further from the result than the closing line; the market is the better forecast.
Same conclusion for totals: neither model beats the close.

correlations.relationship: point margin vs game total (same game)
correlations.reading: Different windows, same conclusion: the two are effectively independent, so a spread+total parlay is priced close to independent legs.

conflicts.this_pipeline: Consensus closing spread/total/moneyline mirrored from nflverse for 2005-2026; labelled consensus, not an official book quote.
conflicts.companion: No official NFL odds/closing-line source is reachable here and none is stored in the repo; model numbers are NOT edges against a market and must not be treated as such.
conflicts.resolution: Superseded by the integration pipeline. Companion pages that state no closing lines exist are accurate for their inputs, not for the repo as it stands now; see Flagged F13.

conflicts.item: Week 10 model margin for WAS @ NYG
conflicts.resolution: Two different rating systems on the same inputs. Both are inside the model's own error band, which is why neither is promoted.
